title: Best Mini PCs in 2026
summary: Eight mini PCs and barebone kits on Newegg, and the questions worth answering before you decide a small box can replace a tower.
body_markdown:
A mini PC has been sitting under my monitor for about two years now, doing everything a tower used to do except play games. I keep expecting to miss the tower. I do not. What I do notice is how many people buy one for the wrong reason and end up disappointed, so let me go through the questions that actually decide this.


## Can a Mini PC Replace a Desktop?


For work, browsing, media and light creative tasks, comfortably. The processors in these boxes are laptop parts or, in a couple of cases, full desktop chips, and the gap to a mid-range tower has mostly closed for anything that is not graphics-heavy.


Where a mini PC does not replace a desktop is gaming. None of these accept a full-size graphics card in the usual way, so you are working with integrated graphics. The strongest here is the Radeon 890M in the[MINISFORUM X1 Pro-470](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856984004?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) , built around a Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with twelve cores, twenty-four threads and a 5.2GHz maximum, rated at up to 86 TOPS overall, with Wi-Fi 7, DDR5-5600 support up to 128GB, three M.2 slots and an SD card reader in a 195 x 195 x 42.5mm chassis.


## Do I Have to Supply My Own Memory and Storage?


Often, yes, and this catches people out. Several of these are barebone kits, which means a chassis, a board and a processor, with the memory and drive left to you.


Ryzen 7 8845HS and a Radeon 780M in a 707 gram box. Memory and drive not included.


The[MINISFORUM UM880 Pro](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856984012?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) is the example I would point at. A Ryzen 7 8845HS with eight cores, sixteen threads and a 5.1GHz maximum, Radeon 780M graphics, two SO-DIMM slots taking DDR5-5600 up to 96GB, two M.2 2280 PCIe 4.0 slots supporting up to 4TB each, dual 2.5 Gbps Ethernet, Wi-Fi 6E and two USB4 ports carrying 8K output, in 66.6 x 130 x 127mm at 707 grams on a 120W supply. It arrives with no memory and no drive.


The[MINISFORUM MS-A2](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856984010?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) comes the other way, with 64GB of DDR5 already installed alongside a Ryzen 9 9955HX at sixteen cores and thirty-two threads up to 5.4GHz, a 10G SFP+ port next to two 2.5G Ethernet ports, and one M.2 or U.2 slot taking up to 15TB plus two more M.2 slots. Storage is still up to you.


## Which One Is Actually Upgradeable?


A real AM5 socket in a 6.1-inch cube. The processor is yours to choose and yours to change.


This is where the ASRock kits separate themselves. The[ASRock DeskMini X600W](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856158097?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) has an actual AM5 socket, taking Ryzen 9000, 8000 or 7000 series processors, two SO-DIMM slots for DDR5-6400 up to 96GB, one M.2 2280 PCIe Gen5 x4 slot and one Gen4 x4 slot, 2.5G Ethernet and a 500W supply, in a 6.1 x 6.1 x 3.15 inch chassis.


The[ASRock DeskSlim X600](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856158101?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) goes further in an unusual direction: four full-size DIMM slots taking DDR5-7200 up to 256GB, AM5 processors up to 120W, a PCIe Gen5 x16 slot, USB4, and a 240W adapter in a 3.74 x 9.25 x 8.66 inch case. It is the closest thing here to a small desktop rather than a large appliance.


The[MINISFORUM MS-A1](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856984007?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) also uses an AM5 socket, shipping with a Ryzen 9 9950X at sixteen cores and 5.7GHz, 64GB of DDR5, four M.2 slots and an OCuLink port, at 1.8 kg.


## What About Intel Options?


A 1.51 pound box with Wi-Fi 7, dual 2.5G Ethernet and a PCIe Gen5 M.2 slot.


The[ASUS NUC 16 Pro](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856110376?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) is a barebone kit built around a Core Ultra 7 356H, sixteen cores in a 6P+8E+4LP arrangement, with two SO-DIMM slots taking DDR5-7200 up to 128GB, one PCIe Gen5 x4 M.2 slot and one Gen4 x4 slot each supporting up to 8TB, dual 2.5 Gbps Ethernet, Wi-Fi 7 with Bluetooth 6.0, and a three-year warranty. It measures 1.65 x 5.67 x 4.61 inches and weighs 1.51 lbs.


The[MSI Cubi NUC AI+ 3MG](https://www.newegg.com/p/N82E16856167219?utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) is the smallest machine here at 4.71 x 4.54 x 1.48 inches and 1.1 lbs, running a Core Ultra 9 386H with sixteen cores in a 4P+8E+4LP layout, dual Intel I226-V 2.5G Ethernet, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 and two Thunderbolt 4 ports, with one M.2 slot and support for up to 64GB of memory.


## So Which Would I Buy?


Everyday desktop replacement, quiet, small: UM880 Pro, with your own memory and drive. Home lab or anything wanting fast networking: MS-A2 for the 10G SFP+ port. A machine you intend to keep and upgrade for years: DeskMini X600W, or DeskSlim X600 if you want a PCIe slot. Smallest possible footprint: MSI Cubi NUC AI+. Balanced Intel build with current wireless: ASUS NUC 16 Pro. Most capable integrated graphics: X1 Pro-470.


The mistake I see most often is buying a barebone kit without budgeting for memory and a drive, then discovering the total is higher than a comparable laptop. Check the listing carefully for what is installed. The full range is in Newegg’s[mini PC listings](https://www.newegg.com/p/pl?d=mini+pc&utm_source=insider&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=insider_article_best-mini-pcs-2026) .


## Frequently Asked Questions


**What does barebone mean when buying a mini PC?** It means the unit ships as a chassis, motherboard and usually a processor, with no memory, no storage and no operating system. The MINISFORUM UM880 Pro and X1 Pro-470, and both ASRock DeskMini and DeskSlim kits, are sold this way. Budget for SO-DIMM memory and an M.2 drive on top of the unit itself.


**Can I play games on a mini PC?** Light games and older titles, yes, on the stronger integrated graphics like the Radeon 890M in the X1 Pro-470 or the Radeon 780M in the UM880 Pro. Modern demanding games are out of reach, since none of these accept a conventional desktop graphics card. If gaming is the point, a small tower is the better shape.


**Do mini PCs use laptop parts or desktop parts?** Both, depending on the model. The MINISFORUM UM880 Pro, X1 Pro-470 and MS-A2 use mobile processors, as do the ASUS and MSI units. The ASRock DeskMini X600W, DeskSlim X600 and MINISFORUM MS-A1 use a full AM5 socket that takes desktop Ryzen processors, which is why they are physically larger and need bigger power supplies.


**How much memory can these take?** It varies more than you would expect. The MSI Cubi NUC AI+ supports up to 64GB, the UM880 Pro and MS-A2 up to 96GB, the ASUS NUC 16 Pro and X1 Pro-470 up to 128GB, and the ASRock DeskSlim X600 up to 256GB across four full-size DIMM slots. Check the slot type as well, since SO-DIMM and full-size DIMM modules are not interchangeable.


**Is dual Ethernet worth having at home?** For most people, no. It matters if you are running a firewall, a home server, or separating networks. Several models here have it, including the UM880 Pro, MS-A1, ASUS NUC 16 Pro and MSI Cubi NUC AI+. The MS-A2 goes further with a 10G SFP+ port, which is genuinely useful only if you already have 10G equipment.
